firstMismatch.behavior: On ordinary D1, the stone giant drops a boulder onto its pit. C prints ‘The boulder fills a pit.’, deletes the trap, consumes the boulder, buries objects, redraws the square, and returns true. JavaScript refuses during preflight before reaching its existing matching flooreffects implementation.

summary: The first missing event is the ordinary boulder-on-pit floor effect. C drops the inventory item through dropx/dropy/dropz into flooreffects; JavaScript's preflight blanket-rejects boulders at every trap, including the already-ported pit and hole branch.

source.branch: do.c:flooreffects first handles a boulder on a PIT or HOLE after the pool-boulder arm. It may report trapped occupants, prints the boulder landing result, deletes any remaining floor trap, consumes the boulder, buries objects, redraws the map square, and returns true. do.c:dropx detaches the item, checks shipping and altar behavior, then calls dropy; dropy calls dropz; dropz invokes flooreffects before ordinary placement. In js/do.js the corresponding flooreffects arm already implements these operations, but preflight_dropx throws for any trap whenever the dropped item is a boulder, before dropx can reach that code.

evidence: The accepted v65 evaluation reports 362/407 screens, 3664/3678 RNG entries, and 362/407 cursors for the case. The manifested source outcome at step 362 is ‘You drop an uncursed boulder. The boulder fills a pit.’
The saved JS runtime diagnostic reaches UnsupportedHeroCommandBoundaryError with ‘unsupported drop: shipping or floor effects at a trap’ after 362 matched screens and 3664 RNG entries.
nethack-c/upstream/src/do.c:dropx, dropy, and dropz establish the production call chain; do.c:flooreffects lines 188-266 contain the boulder pit/hole arm before the hero pit-edge arm.
js/do.js:flooreffects lines 1006-1138 implements the C boulder-on-pit/hole result. js/do.js:preflight_dropx lines 1955-1963 instead rejects every boulder at a trap before that implementation can run.
Existing scripts/drop-command.test.mjs assertions encode this blanket refusal and will be revised only for C-supported paths; the C source defines other traps as inert in flooreffects.
